inputs.original_text: This flare-up between the US, Israel, and Iran is sending oil prices skyrocketing and squeezing fuel costs right here in India. The government's move to cut excise duties and keep petrol and diesel from jumping is nothing but reckless short-term interference that bleeds away national revenue and sets the stage for worse inflation later. Our heavy dependence on foreign crude imports has left the country exposed to these endless overseas conflicts, and it's time we stopped pretending global meddling can fix what only real national strength can. We should be putting energy self-reliance and sovereignty first, along with the old-fashioned values of prudence, personal responsibility, and family security that built stable societies in the first place, instead of chaining ourselves to unstable foreign powers that threaten our economic order and the future of our households.
inputs.modified_text: This flare-up between the US, Israel, and Iran is driving oil prices through the roof and putting serious pressure on fuel costs here in India. Rather than tackling the underlying vulnerability, the government's reckless decision to cut excise duties on petrol and diesel to prevent prices from rising is just short-term meddling that drains our national revenue and will only fuel worse inflation down the line. Our reliance on foreign crude imports has exposed us to the chaos of these foreign conflicts. It's clear we can no longer rely on global entanglements to protect us; only a strong, sovereign nation can. We need to focus on achieving energy self-reliance to safeguard our sovereignty and uphold the traditional principles of prudence, personal responsibility, and family security that have always been the foundation of stable societies. Continuing to depend on unstable foreign powers will only undermine our economic stability and put the future of our families at risk.
